Two of the ten baseline files scored by the like-for-like check are untracked at the repository root
by a deliberate, committed decision (EVID-01, commit `707923c`). That reading therefore re-runs on a
tree holding them and **not on a fresh clone**. Recorded under D-48-C rather than closed, because
closing it would overturn a researched, cited and verified decision.

## [9.4.0] — 2026-09-20

Milestone release: **v9.4.0 Claim Correction and Gate Relaxation**. The milestone opened as
*Source-Literal Pinning* and was renamed at close. Its own pre-registered kill switch — PRE-2, the
marginal apparatus cost of a product edit, fixed at 6.8:1 at `c571ccf` before the first edit — read
**STOP** at the end of Phase 37, so Phase 38 (Anchor Derivation) never started and the verdict was
not re-taken to rescue it. Phase 39 was not started and returns to the backlog. The name now
describes what shipped rather than what was attempted; `docs/v9.4-source-literal-pin-relaxation.md`
holds the M3 record and its landing readings, including the STOP.

Phases 40–45 already shipped inside `[9.3.1]`, `[9.3.2]` and `[9.3.3]`. New in this release: Phase
46's exemplar corrections, and the Phase 36/37 apparatus work.

Closes backlog **999.124** and **999.126** as a **product change**: the shipped worked exemplars
(`shared/examples/*.md`, emitted to `first-principles/agents/references/examples/`) are brought
current and their Phase 44 gap-closure residuals corrected. Every figure was re-derived by hand
before it was written, and each restatement site moved with its origin.

Names the edited surfaces:

- [`self-application.md`](first-principles/agents/references/examples/self-application.md) — dated
  rather than re-authored (999.124). It now opens with an **As of this analysis** stamp naming
  2026-05-24 and commit `e5063b3`, disclosing that GT-6's wording was added later and describes a
  v8.17.3 tree, and closes with a re-measured Outcome postscript. All eighteen `878`-line sites and
  every chain are kept intact, so the analysis still reproduces against the tree it was written
  against; `git show e5063b3:first-principles/agents/first-principles.md | wc -l` returns 878, which
  makes the stamp's falsifiability offer real rather than decorative. Outcome check 2 states that
  both of its heading patterns matched **at `e5063b3`**, so its zero result against the current body
  reads as a measurement rather than a pattern that never matched; Outcome check 3 separates the
  seven live links from the one prose citation at body line 325 and publishes a second re-runnable
  command. GT-7's `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md` citation is disclosed as never-trackable.
- [`software-systems.md`](first-principles/agents/references/examples/software-systems.md) — the
  runner reduction is bounded to its stated overhead, test-suite time is no longer called pipeline
  time, and the dead end and section 6 are made conditional (RF-05, RF-06, RF-10, RF-11). Section
  6's profiling precondition is separated from the branches it selects between, and the premise the
  5–10% runner cap silently assumed is named.
- [`estimate-fermi.md`](first-principles/agents/references/examples/estimate-fermi.md) — the
  "consistent with GT-5" claim is narrowed to what the figures support, the O&M reserve is
  propagated to every driver site, the installed-capital label is split from its O&M-inclusive
  figure, and the basis for widening the cycle-life bracket past its cited source is named
  (RF-07, RF-08, WR-01, WR-02, WR-04).
- [`science-engineering-2.md`](first-principles/agents/references/examples/science-engineering-2.md)
  — the 18 mm contact figure's actual origin is named instead of disclaimed, the figure is bound to
  its role in the GT-2? counter-figure, and the counter-figure sentence is unnested so its subject
  reaches its verb (RF-12, WR-06, IN-03).

**Apparatus.** `scripts/check-act-limb.py` now matches whitespace-flexibly throughout, and 21 of its
33 incidental sub-assertions are section-scoped rather than paragraph-scoped — every converted site's
originating defect proven to still fail by name, and the 11 sub-assertions that mutation testing
measured load-bearing kept on block scope. All 36 sub-assertions were classified by mutation
evidence, not judgement (25 incidental / 11 load-bearing), recorded in
`tests/pin-classification-v9.4/` and `tests/pin-conversion-v9.4/`. Refining the prose that carries
the methodology is correspondingly cheaper, though by how much is not claimed: PRE-2 read STOP.

The registered gate set is unchanged in this release — battery **23**, CI **19**, both by direct
count. The retirements that moved those totals from 26 and 23 shipped in `[9.3.1]`.

input.prompt:
Analyze this design decision from first principles.

Context: We maintain a Claude Code plugin. It ships a single agent file that inlines: the core methodology body, six companion-tool procedures, an output template, and a validation rubric. Two milestones after the file shipped, it measured 878 lines, against a recorded budget of ~500 lines / ~5,000 tokens that is enforced as a regression gate in the project's CI/test suite. The budget is nominally violated by about 75%.

The reflexive engineering response is: split the file, extracting content into separate reference files that get pulled in on demand.

# v9.4 Gate Retirement

**Milestone:** v9.4.0 (Phase 40)
**Recorded:** 2026-09-15
**Phase base:** `dc84840`
**Status:** Standing governing record. Successor to
[docs/v8.7-constraint-teardown.md](v8.7-constraint-teardown.md) under that record's §4 procedure.

---

## 1. Scope and Standing

This is the D-01 successor governing record for Phase 40, naming
[`v8.7-constraint-teardown.md`](v8.7-constraint-teardown.md) as the record it succeeds and
following that record's §4 procedure step by step, once per retired or relaxed item.

This is a **subtraction record against a default-frozen baseline**. Anything not explicitly
named in §2 below stays frozen and gating by default — silence never means permission. A future
milestone finding this document silent on a constraint it wants to touch must treat that silence
as "still frozen," the same rule `v8.7-constraint-teardown.md` §1 states for itself.

**D-02 — this record is separate from the source-literal pinning phase's relaxation record.**
That record's parent is [`v8.5-byte-freeze-relaxation.md`](v8.5-byte-freeze-relaxation.md) §4, and
its procedure is distinct from this one. The two are not merged: this record follows
`v8.7-constraint-teardown.md`'s "What Is Retired" shape, the other follows
`v8.5-byte-freeze-relaxation.md`'s "What Is Relaxed" shape, and each names its own predecessor.

**D-04 — both predecessor records stay byte-intact.** No in-place edit is made to
`docs/v8.7-constraint-teardown.md` or `docs/v8.5-byte-freeze-relaxation.md`, including to the
teardown record's own §5 battery-composition text. Every correction to either record's substance
is stated here, in this successor record, instead.

**REACH-or-LEVEL, answered in writing (standing instruction 3).** A retirement is neither. It adds
no guard and widens no existing guard's reach over more product surface — it removes a check and,
where a replacement is warranted, moves an assertion of a real property onto an *existing* gate
(REG-GUARD) rather than building a new one. `docs/PROCESS.md` §1.1's own test — REACH points an
existing product-guard at more product surface; LEVEL adds a guard whose subject is another
guard's own correctness — does not classify a subtraction at all; nothing here is scored as either.

**No ordering constraint against the source-literal pinning work.** The six scripts named below
hold none of the literals the source-literal pinning milestone's pre-registered census counts
(checked at Phase 40's opening against that milestone's own pivot record), so this phase carries no
sequencing dependency on that work and may land before, after, or interleaved with it.

**D-09 — provenance, not evidence of record.** The 2026-09-13 filing readings (at commit `2c3f0c1`)
are cited below only as where a finding originated. Every reading quoted as evidence in §2 was
re-measured at this phase's own base commit, `dc84840`, on 2026-09-15.

---

## 2. What Is Retired

Six items. Each subsection names the item, quotes measured evidence at phase base `dc84840`,
states the decision and its rationale, states exactly what is superseded, names the remaining
owner of the property (if any survives), and reserves a `#### Landing readings` heading that the
plan performing that item's own retirement fills with its own commit's evidence.

### 2.1 COLLIDE-01 — dual-install name-collision scan (backlog 999.106)

**Named item.** `scripts/check-install-collisions.py`, gate id `COLLIDE-01`, registered in CI
(`check-install-collisions (COLLIDE-01)`), the offline battery (`gate "COLLIDE-01"`), and
`scripts/_gate_registry.py`.

**Measured evidence.** The live scan, re-run at base:

```
$ python3 scripts/check-install-collisions.py
check-install-collisions: PASS (plugin names: 15, monolith names: 0, no name collisions)
```

`monolith names: 0` is not an incidental reading — the v2.x monolith install surface this gate
was built to guard against was removed at `3fd5287` (v3.0.0), well before this gate's own
registration at v7.9. There is no second install surface left to collide against, by construction,
not by luck of the current tree state.

The self-test, unaffected by this fact, still passes on its own synthetic fixture:

```
$ python3 scripts/check-install-collisions.py --self-test
check-install-collisions --self-test: PASS (fixture collision detected: 'first-principles'; disjoint pair clean; collector fixture flagged 'shared-tool'; describe() consistency control: registered_surfaces moved with PLUGIN_DIR)
```

The M1 mutation table (both sub-mutations run in a scratch worktree at `dc84840`, restored after):

| sub-mutation | COLLIDE-01 | REG-GUARD | GATE-01 |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) skill `name:` set to a duplicate/wrong value | PASS | FAIL | PASS |
| (b) agent `name:` set to a wrong value | PASS | FAIL | FAIL |

COLLIDE-01 never catches either mutation. Its own live scan is vacuous (`monolith names: 0` in
both runs) — it can only ever compare the plugin's names against an absent second surface, so no
edit anywhere in the plugin tree can produce a cross-surface overlap for it to catch. REG-GUARD
catches both mutations (its `verify_skill_names` and agent-name check read every stub's and the
agent's own frontmatter value directly); GATE-01 (`check-agent.py`) catches only the agent-name
mutation, since it validates only the agent file.

**Decision and rationale.** Retire outright. The property `docs/CONFIGURATION.md:186` names this
gate as enforcing — "`name` in frontmatter must match the parent directory name exactly" — was
never this gate's actual check (a cross-surface collision scan, not a name-vs-directory check),
and the M1 table above shows that property is already owned entirely by REG-GUARD and GATE-01. No
replacement assertion is proposed, because there is no second install surface for a replacement to
compare against; inventing one would recreate exactly the "guard nothing real" shape being
retired.

**What is superseded.** CI job `check-install-collisions (COLLIDE-01)`; the battery call
`gate "COLLIDE-01" ...`; `scripts/_gate_registry.py`'s `COLLIDE-01` entry; `docs/gates/COLLIDE-01.md`;
`scripts/check-install-collisions.py`; the two `scripts/trace-tests-usage.py` `GATE_COMMANDS`
tuples that subprocess-invoke it; matrix rows `v7.9/COLLIDE-01` and `v7.9/COLLIDE-02`
(re-tiered audit-only — see §5); the `docs/CONFIGURATION.md:186` sentence naming COLLIDE-01 as the
name-vs-directory enforcer.

**Remaining owner.** The property M1 actually exercises — frontmatter `name:` matching its
directory, for both skills and the agent — is owned by REG-GUARD (`scripts/check-registration.py`,
`verify_skill_names` and the agent-name check) and by GATE-01 (`scripts/check-agent.py`, agent
file only). Both already hold this property today; nothing new is added to either.

1	<!-- GENERATED — DO NOT EDIT. Source: shared/examples/self-application.md. Regenerate via: scripts/sync-content.py --write. -->
2	
3	# Worked Example: Self-Application (Meta)
4	
5	A complete first-principles analysis applied to a live, contested design decision
6	*about the agent that performs first-principles analyses*. The triggering observation
7	is that `first-principles/agents/first-principles.md` was 878 lines at the time of
8	this analysis, while META-Q4 records a budget of "~500 lines / ~5,000 tokens."
9	Authored in Phase 32 as a dogfooding example: the methodology turned on the artifact
10	it ships from.
11	
12	**As of this analysis:** the Ground Truths below were measured on 2026-05-24 against
13	the tree at commit `e5063b3` (`feat(32-02): add self-application worked example`),
14	with one exception noted in GT-6 itself: its "Described rather than reproduced" note
15	and its link-form parenthetical were added on 2026-08-16 by commit `9e11072` and
16	describe a v8.17.3 tree, not the `e5063b3` one, so a reader who checks out `e5063b3`
17	will find GT-6's wording there differs. That anchor commit
18	recorded three premises this analysis reasons from: the agent body was 878
19	lines, the Output Template and Validation Rubric appendices were inlined into that
20	body, and the META-Q4 budget gate was binding on every change. A reader can check
21	out `e5063b3` and re-run `wc -l first-principles/agents/first-principles.md` to
22	confirm the 878 figure directly, rather than take this stamp's word for it. The tree
23	has since changed; see the dated Outcome section at the end of this file for what
24	happened.
25	
26	**Scenario.** The single-agent surface shipped in v3.0 inlined the methodology body,
27	the six companion-tool procedures, the canonical output template, and the validation
28	rubric into one file at `first-principles/agents/first-principles.md`. Two milestones
29	later the file measured 878 lines. The recorded budget — `~500 lines / ~5,000
30	tokens`, encoded as regression gate META-Q4 in `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md` — is
31	nominally violated by roughly 75%. Engineering convention reaches reflexively for
32	the response *"split it"* (extract content into `references/` files). This analysis
33	strips that response away and asks what the budget is actually optimizing for before
34	choosing any intervention.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## 1. Problem Essence
39	
40	**Core problem:** What does the ~500-line agent-body budget optimize for, does the
41	current 878-line body violate that optimization in a measurable way, and what is
42	the minimum intervention — if any is warranted — that restores the property the
43	budget exists to protect?
44	
45	The triggering framing — "the body is too long, how should we split it?" — is a
46	proposed solution sitting on top of an unverified premise: that the ~500-line
47	budget is load-bearing for some property of the agent, and that 878 lines breaks
48	that property. First-principles analysis requires interrogating the budget itself
49	before reasoning about extractions. The symptom is "over budget"; the underlying
50	question is whether the budget tracks anything the agent actually depends on.
51	
52	**Success criteria:**
53	
54	- The property the ~500-line budget exists to protect is named explicitly and
55	  traced to a shipped artifact (REQUIREMENTS.md, PROJECT.md, or a regression gate),
56	  not asserted from general best-practice intuition.
57	- The 878-line body is decomposed into structural segments with measured line
58	  ranges so that "which segment is consuming the budget" is a checkable fact, not
59	  a guess.
60	- The recommended intervention — if any — addresses the segment that actually
61	  drives the overage, not the segment that is most syntactically tempting to
62	  extract.
63	- If the budget turns out to be a stale convention whose underlying property no
64	  longer holds, the recommendation revises the budget rather than performing an
65	  extraction that solves nothing.
66	- The recommendation does not prejudge the v3.0 inlining decision; if the
67	  inlining was correct then and remains correct now, the conclusion says so.
68	
69	---
70	
71	## 2. Assumptions Table
72	
73	| Assumption | Type | Treatment | Verdict | Verification |
74	|------------|------|-----------|---------|--------------|
75	| The ~500-line budget is load-bearing for some observable property of the agent | untested belief | Verify before use — locate the artifact that records the budget and the property it protects; if the property is not specified, the budget is a convention, not a constraint | Challenge — the protected property is unnamed; META-Q4 records only the number, with no independent measurable consequence | Recorded in `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md` line 53 as META-Q4; the protected property is named as "stays under the ~500-line / ~5,000-token budget" with rationale "New content lives in references/" — i.e., the budget is itself the property, with no independent measurable consequence stated; flagged for further classification |
76	| The agent body is too long because the methodology procedure is too long | untested belief — diagnostic | Verify by ruling out alternative segments — multiple structural sections could individually account for the overage; collecting confirming evidence for "the methodology is bloated" is not the same as ruling out the appendices, the companion-tool procedures, or accumulated cross-references | Challenge — unverified; requires line-range measurement of the body's segments before naming the dominant contributor | Unverified — flagged; line-range measurement of the body's structural segments (Section 3, GT-2 through GT-4) is required before any segment can be named as the dominant contributor |
77	| Aggressive Layer-3 extraction of Phase 1–5 procedural blocks would bring the body under 500 lines | untested belief — methodology | Verify by constructing the alternative — measure the procedural-block line range and compute the resulting body size if the extraction were performed | Discard — extraction saves only ~96 lines, leaving the body 282 lines over budget (chain C2) | Phase 1–5 procedural blocks span lines 45–141 of `first-principles/agents/first-principles.md` (~96 lines). Extracting them yields a body of approximately 782 lines, still 282 lines over budget — the proposed method does not produce the claimed outcome (Chain 2 in Section 4) |
78	| Extracting content into `references/` always reduces the agent's reasoning quality | convention — context-dependent technical | Challenge specifically by naming the contextual variables — what kind of content, when read by the agent, with what frequency, under what continuation properties | Challenge — no observed regression from the one existing external reference; the convention holds only for unconditionally-inspected content | The agent body already delegates the Subtype Catalog to `references/assumption-taxonomy.md` (line 92 cross-reference) without an observed reasoning regression. The convention holds only for content the agent must inspect on every single analysis; content the agent looks up conditionally does not appear bound by it |
79	| The v3.0 inlining decision must be preserved as-shipped | convention — default-response | Challenge by asking whether "preserve the shipped surface" addresses the highest-frequency observed signal versus the cognitively-available response. The v3.0 inlining was justified for *the methodology and companion tools*; the inlining of the Output Template and Validation Rubric appendices is a separate decision that has not been independently scrutinized | Challenge — the v3.0 rationale names methodology and companion tools, not the appendix re-inlining | The PROJECT.md v3.0 rationale (`shared/spine/references` → "absorb their methodology, companion-tool references, and worked examples into the agent's reachable context") names methodology + companion tools + examples; it does not separately justify inlining the Layer-3 appendices that were already authored as Layer-3 reference files |
80	| A full rewrite or large body restructure is required to bring the budget into compliance | untested belief — false-dichotomy | Challenge the binary framing — enumerate intermediate options (extract one block, extract two appendices, revise the budget, do nothing) and check whether any dominates the poles on cost and reversibility | Discard — a de-inlining intermediate exists and dominates the rewrite on reversibility (chain C3) | At least one intermediate option (de-inline the Output Template and Validation Rubric appendices, leaving methodology and companion tools intact) is testable for body-size impact in Chain 3 and dominates the rewrite on reversibility |
81	
82	---
83	
84	## 3. Ground Truths
85	
86	- **GT-1** The agent body file `first-principles/agents/first-principles.md` is
87	  currently 878 lines as measured by `wc -l` at the time of this analysis — source:
88	  direct measurement of the file in this repository on the working branch.
89	
90	- **GT-2** The procedural body (the methodology proper — Phases 1–5 entry/operation/
91	  artifact/exit blocks plus the "How the phases connect" preamble) spans lines
92	  45–141 of the agent body, approximately 96 lines — source: heading scan of
93	  `first-principles/agents/first-principles.md` (`## Methodology` at line 45;
94	  `## Output format` at line 142 marks the next top-level heading).
95	
96	- **GT-3** The inlined companion-tool procedures (six `## Procedure` blocks for
97	  5-Whys, fishbone, inversion, pre-mortem, trade-off, second-order) span lines
98	  234–408, approximately 175 lines — source: heading scan of the same file
99	  (six `## Procedure` headings at lines 234, 259, 291, 320, 345, 376; next
100	  top-level heading `## How to Use This Template` at line 415 marks the appendix
101	  boundary).
102	
103	- **GT-4** Two Layer-3 reference files exist as separate artifacts under
104	  `shared/spine/references/`: `output-template.md` (150 lines) and
105	  `validation-rubric.md` (320 lines). Together these contain 470 lines of
106	  authored Layer-3 reference content that already lives outside the agent body
107	  in the source-of-truth tree — source: direct `wc -l` measurement of both files
108	  and inspection of the repository layout.
109	
110	- **GT-5** The agent body inlines the same Output Template and Validation Rubric
111	  content as appendices: `## How to Use This Template` begins at line 415 and the
112	  appendix region runs to line 878 (the end of the file), approximately 464 lines.

240	lift each phase into its own Layer-3 reference file under
241	`shared/spine/references/`. The motivation was that the procedural blocks are
242	the most explicitly "procedural" — they read like a recipe — and procedural
243	content is conventionally the kind that benefits most from being externalized

259	**Why abandoned:** Three failures, each independently sufficient.
260	
261	First, GT-2 measures the Phase 1–5 procedural blocks at approximately 96 lines.
262	Extracting them in full saves at most ~96 lines and leaves the body at
263	approximately 782 lines — still 282 lines over META-Q4 (the constraint the
264	extraction was supposed to satisfy). The chain "Phase 1–5 is too long → extract

268	would actually move the body under budget — and the appendix extraction is the

271	Second, the procedural through-line is the part of the agent body the agent

274	Assumptions Table is built on top of the Essence Statement"). Pushing each

283	content benefits from externalization" do not collapse the difference between
284	conditional reference content and unconditional procedural content.

347	## 6. Conclusion
348	
349	**Recommended approach:** (chains C1, C2 and C3) Execute one configuration-level intervention and
350	commission one measurement, in parallel.
351	
352	1. **De-inline the Output Template and Validation Rubric appendices** (chain C3) from
353	   `first-principles/agents/first-principles.md`. Replace the appendix region
354	   (currently lines 415–878) with two one-line external references in the
355	   `### Reference docs` block that already exists at line 226: a link to
356	   `references/output-template.md` and a link to `references/validation-rubric.md`.
357	   These reference files already exist in `shared/spine/references/` and already
358	   propagate to the agent surface via `scripts/sync-content.py`. The intervention
359	   is authored in `shared/` (the body source) and synced; no hand-edit of the
360	   agent surface occurs. Expected body size after the change: approximately
361	   414 lines, comfortably under the META-Q4 budget of ~500. The intervention is
362	   fully reversible by reverting the body edit.
363	
364	2. **Commission the GT-9? measurement** (chain C1) that would settle whether body-size
365	   reduction *matters* for agent reasoning quality. The minimum form is a
366	   small A/B: run the EVAL-01 climbing-gym fixture (or an equivalent rigor
367	   probe) against both the pre-intervention 878-line body and the
368	   post-intervention ~414-line body, holding model and prompt fixed. If the
369	   measurement shows no rigor difference, META-Q4 should be re-recorded as a
370	   heuristic with the measurement attached; if it shows a rigor improvement,
371	   META-Q4's binding force is verified and the intervention is doubly
372	   justified; if it shows a regression, the intervention is reverted before
373	   it ships.
374	
375	The intervention is justified independently of the measurement's outcome
376	because it deduplicates content that the source tree already contains in
377	two places (the inlined appendix region of the agent body, and the
378	authored Layer-3 reference files under `shared/spine/references/`). The
379	measurement is justified independently of the intervention because META-Q4
380	will continue to fire on every future content addition and the gate's
381	binding force should be settled rather than inherited from convention.
382	
383	**Key insight:** (chains C1 and C2) The cognitively-available response to "the agent body is
384	878 lines vs. a ~500-line budget" is to extract the most procedural-looking
385	content — the Phase 1–5 methodology blocks. That response is wrong on
386	arithmetic before any reasoning-quality argument is made: the methodology
387	proper is ~96 lines and its extraction leaves the body at ~782 lines, still
388	282 lines over budget. The 464 lines of inlined appendix content — content
389	that already exists as Layer-3 reference files in the source tree and is
390	duplicated verbatim into the agent body — is what actually consumes the
391	budget. The first-principles move is not "split the body" but "measure
392	which segment consumes the budget, then verify what the budget exists to
393	protect." Once measured, the right segment is unambiguous, the
394	intervention is configuration-level rather than architectural, and the
395	remaining question — whether the budget binds anything observable — is
396	recognized as the real open question rather than collapsed into the
397	extraction problem.
398	
399	**Trade-offs acknowledged:**
400	
401	- (chain C3) The de-inlining intervention costs the agent one additional read hop for
402	  Output Template and Validation Rubric content. The Phase 31 delegation
403	  precedent (GT-6) shows the hop is workable for catalog-style reference
404	  content; the appendices are also Layer-3 reference content (they exist
405	  as standalone reference files in `shared/spine/references/`) and are
406	  thus structurally analogous to the precedent. The trade-off is real but
407	  small and reversible.
408	
409	- (chains C2 and C3) The intervention does not touch the inlined companion-tool procedures
410	  (~175 lines, GT-3) or the Phase 1–5 methodology blocks (~96 lines, GT-2).
411	  Both remain inline. The v3.0 inlining rationale named methodology and
412	  companion tools specifically; this intervention respects that rationale
413	  while interrogating the part of v3.0 that was not separately justified —
414	  the appendix re-inlining of files that already existed as references.
415	
416	- (chain C1) The MEDIUM confidence on chain C1 carries into the recommendation: if the
417	  GT-9? measurement shows the budget tracks nothing measurable, the
418	  intervention is still defensible on deduplication grounds but no longer
419	  has an analytical-rigor justification. The measurement is what
420	  distinguishes a deduplication win from a rigor win; it should not be
421	  deferred indefinitely.
422	
423	- (chains C2 and C3) The recommendation does not perform the more ambitious restructure
424	  candidates that were considered and abandoned (Phase 1–5 extraction,
425	  full rewrite). Those remain available as future moves if measurement
426	  later identifies them as warranted; the false-dichotomy assumption in
427	  Section 2 is discharged by the existence of the de-inlining
428	  intermediate.

# v8.7 Constraint Teardown

**Milestone:** v8.7 Analysis Correctness, Constraint Teardown & Output-Contract Integrity (Phase 163)
**Recorded:** 2026-07-22
**Status:** Standing governing record. Inherited by every future milestone — no expiry, no
v8.7-only scoping.

> **Standing — adjudicated 2026-08-16 (audit stream 3): GOVERNING RECORD — the most heavily
> cited document in `docs/`.** Every retirement it records is still in force, and sixteen
> files cite it as the reason something is the way it is, and they enumerate exactly:
> `CLAUDE.md` (×7); **both** pre-commit hook paths (`.githooks/pre-commit`,
> `scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit`); four scripts — `check-body-budget.py` (×4, including a string
> it prints at runtime), `check-firewall-battery.sh` (×3), `_battery_core.py` (×3),
> `check-traceability.py`; a `gap_rationale` in `docs/data/matrix.json` and its rendered
> `requirements-matrix.md`; and seven `docs/` prose surfaces (`ARCHITECTURE`, `CONFIGURATION`,
> `DATA-FLOW`, `DEVELOPMENT`, `MEASUREMENT-MAP`, `README`, `TESTING`). Nothing resolves it —
> no `artifact_link` points here — but it is the
> single document whose deletion would strand the most live explanations. It governs
> TEARDOWN-01/02/03, the K-of-5-is-an-observation-not-a-gate rule, and the retirement of the
> 644-line body budget. Cite it; do not restate its rules elsewhere. See
> [audit-2026-08-16-duplication-staleness.md](audit-2026-08-16-duplication-staleness.md).

---

## 1. Scope and Standing

This is a **named standing rule**, not a one-off v8.7-scoped exception. It carries no expiry
date. A future milestone reads this record the same way it reads
[`v8.0-final-closure.md`](v8.0-final-closure.md) — as a durable disposition, not a temporary
grant that lapses when v8.7 ships.

The rule is a **subtraction record against a default-frozen baseline**. Anything not explicitly
listed in §2 below remains frozen and gating by default. Silence never means permission — a
future milestone that wants to touch something not named in §2 must author its own successor
record per the procedure in §4, not read this document's silence as authorization.

This record's scope did not originate from a previous milestone's own paperwork — it derives
from the 2026-07-22 `.planning/ALTITUDE.md` constraint audit, which re-examined nine carried
constraints against evidence rather than inheriting them by default. Five were found invalidated
and are retired below; four survived and are restated in §3 as still frozen.

---

## 2. What Is Retired

Exactly five items. No more.

**1. The 644-line body-budget gate.**

The gate is retired; the figure is not. `scripts/check-body-budget.py` still reports the
generated agent body's current line count on every run, but it no longer fails a commit or a
battery run because of that count. The evidence: the script's own fitted-limit provenance
comment — "limit raised to 622 + 22 buffer" — records that the number was recalibrated whenever
it bound, across the raise chain 500 → 580 → 644, rather than derived from any measured quality
requirement. `docs/v8.6-quality-ab-experiment.md`'s blind A/B is the null result that confirms
the fitted number carried no quality signal: a 590-line body and a 612-line body — a 22-line
contrast, the exact size of the "buffer" the limit was raised to protect — scored identically,
both arms 2/3 PASS, band total 35 each, with failures tracking the problem rather than the arm.

Name the irony plainly: v8.6 spent a whole milestone compressing the agent body to buy back
22 lines of headroom under a budget this record now retires, and that same milestone's own A/B
experiment is the evidence that the 22 lines did not matter. What survives: the figure is still
reported — on every `check-body-budget.py` invocation and on every
`check-firewall-battery.sh` run, as an un-tallied `[INFO]` line — because Phase 165 needs the
body's growth to stay visible even though nothing will block it.

**2. The `_COMPOSER_FOCUS_CEILING` freeze — the freeze only.**

The value stays 4. This record grants permission to change `_COMPOSER_FOCUS_CEILING` under a
successor procedure (§4); this phase performs no retune. The evidence:
`docs/v8.6-live-remeasure-verdict.md`'s Phase 160 S-P03 run5 finding, which shows the ceiling
actively penalising fidelity rather than merely gating noise — run5 fired the highest fishbone
marker count of the five runs measured (4 distinct markers, more than any of runs 1–4) and was
still scored a miss, purely because its `composer_hits` count reached
`_COMPOSER_FOCUS_CEILING`. The run that most closely followed the expected template was the one
the ceiling suppressed.

Record honestly: dropping the literal drift guards on the constant does not by itself make it
freely editable in practice. RR-77-08's surviving relative check
(`_rr7708_composer == _COMPOSER_FOCUS_CEILING - 1`) compares an adversarial fixture's
`composer_hits` count against one below the ceiling, and that fixture's hit count is fixed at 3
in the sentinel's own source. A future retune of `_COMPOSER_FOCUS_CEILING` is therefore a
two-part edit — the constant itself and the fixture that proves it is load-bearing — and a
successor record must say so rather than assume changing one constant is sufficient.

**3. K-of-5 Step 0 as a phase gate.**

K-of-5 Step 0 results are recorded observations from here forward; they may not gate a phase.
The evidence: the S-P04 (five-whys) vector 2/5 → 0/5 → 2/5 across v7.11, v8.5, and v8.6 — a
value that swung across the pass/fail line twice with no source change to the five-whys
technique between those measurements that would explain the swing. At N=5, noise equals effect;
a single flipped run moves the recorded K/N by 20 percentage points, which is not a resolution
either direction can be read as durable.

What is demoted is the **authority of the number**, not the tool. `scripts/check-step0-live.py`
is untouched by this phase: it keeps `--min-pass` and its verdict line, because every frozen
baseline from v7.4 through v8.6 and every documented invocation depends on that comparability
staying intact. A future milestone that reruns the harness still gets a K/N and a PASS/FAIL
verdict line from the tool itself — what changes is that this record, and the docs that follow
it, no longer treat that verdict as a gate a phase must clear.

**4. The gitignored-and-unrecoverable posture of one strategic-record path — `matrix.json` only.**

`.planning/phases/82-traceability-matrix-and-gap-findings/matrix.json` is un-ignored by a targeted
`.gitignore` negation (Plan 03 of this phase); `.planning/` stays ignored otherwise, and
`.planning/ALTITUDE.md` specifically **remains ignored and untracked** — its un-ignore is deferred,
not performed, by this phase (see the disposition below). `matrix.json` is tracked as a committed
artifact rather than left to regeneration — regeneration produces a fresh matrix, not
recoverability of the specific frozen artifact that the `phases.clear` workaround (item 5, below)
existed to protect.

> **Amendment (2026-07-28, post-v8.13).** The artifact has been relocated to `docs/data/matrix.json`
> and `.gitignore` restored to a blanket `.planning/` rule. Nothing about item 4's substance
> changes: the matrix JSON is still tracked, still recoverable from `phases.clear`, still

The correctness spot-check (Phase 162) re-derived 65 load-bearing claims across six frozen analyses — 47 correct / 6 wrong / 12 unverifiable, zero material errors, milestone proceeds — but surfaced the more consequential finding: rubric conformance does not predict arithmetic correctness (the most accurate document failed the rubric; the least accurate passed). Constraint teardown (Phase 163) then retired five carried constraints on that evidence: the 644-line body-budget gate, the `_COMPOSER_FOCUS_CEILING=4` freeze, K-of-5 Step 0 as a phase gate, the blanket gitignored-planning posture, and the `phases.clear`-stays-OFF workaround. The output-contract fix (Phase 165) then landed chain-form conversion, a §6→§4 closure check, and a Verdict-token prefix format — five behavior-changing consistency fixes, shipped without a live re-measure of Step 0 or routing (an explicitly accepted caveat). The post-fix blind re-measure (Phase 166) returned an honest **MIXED** verdict: the untraced-defect incidence held flat at 6/6, chain-defect incidence improved 6/6 to 4/6, and the aggregate +9 band delta shrank to roughly +3 once drift noise was controlled for — the real signal is the chain-rigor improvement, not the aggregate. # First-Principles Analysis: The ~500-Line Agent-Body Budget vs. the Reflexive "Split It" Response

**Note on delivery:** this task is running under explicit instructions for this invocation ("do NOT write report/summary/analysis `.md` files — return findings directly as your final message"), which overrides the skill's default file/PDF-delivery pipeline. What follows is the complete analysis delivered as text, in the six-section shape, without the file-writing/figure/PDF apparatus.

**Grounding note:** the repo is reachable (`/home/chrisdavidson/Projects/first-principles-skill`), and — this is the load-bearing fact — **this exact scenario already happened in it, was already analyzed first-principles-style, was executed, and was then independently re-tested and extended by later, unrelated project milestones.** I did not need to reason about this in the abstract; I verified the actual file, the actual gate code, the actual retirement records, and the actual measured experiment. Every Ground Truth below cites where I read it.

---

## 1. Problem Essence

**Core problem:** What property was the ~500-line/~5,000-token agent-body budget actually meant to protect; did the 878-line (and now 1,424-line) body actually violate that property, measurably; and is the correct response to split the file, leave it, change the number, or something else?

**Success criteria:**
- The protected property is named from an actual artifact (requirement, gate definition, or governing record), not asserted from "long files are bad" intuition.
- The current body is decomposed into measured segments so "what's actually driving growth" is a checkable fact.
- The recommendation targets whatever segment/mechanism measurement shows is real, not whatever looks most "procedural" to extract.
- If the budget is a stale, unmeasured convention, the recommendation says so and revises the gate rather than performing an extraction that fixes nothing.
- The recommendation does not assume the v3.0 inlining decision was wrong merely because a number now reads red.

---

## 2. Assumptions Table

| Assumption | Type | Treatment | Verdict | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| The line/token budget is load-bearing for some observable property of the agent | untested belief | Locate the artifact naming the protected property | **Discard as stated** | The original requirement (quoted in GT-1, itself unverifiable since its source file was never tracked) records only "stays under ~500 lines/~5,000 tokens. New content lives in references/" — the number *is* the requirement; no independent consequence is named anywhere in `docs/` (GT-9, GT-10) |
| Body growth beyond X lines degrades the agent's reasoning quality | untested belief | Find or commission a direct measurement | **Tested and falsified within the measured range** | A blind A/B at 590 vs. 612 lines scored identically — 2/3 PASS, band total 35, mean 11.67, both arms (GT-3) |
| The body is long because the methodology procedure itself is bloated | untested belief — diagnostic | Measure segment line ranges before targeting an extraction | **Discard** | Current inlined companion-tool procedures are 8 blocks (GT-8); the historically measured overage driver was 464 lines of *duplicated* appendix content, not the core procedure (prior self-application analysis, GT-11) |
| Splitting into reference files always helps | convention — context-dependent | Challenge by asking what kind of content, read how often | **Challenge, partially true** | True for content read conditionally (the appendices, now externalized, GT-8); the project's own abandoned-reasoning record found it false for the unconditional Phase 1–5 procedural through-line (GT-11) |
| "Split the file" and "leave it as-is" are the only two options | untested belief — false dichotomy | Enumerate intermediates/composites | **Discard** | What was actually done was a composite: externalize only the duplicated segment, retire the numeric gate, and replace it with a direct quality instrument (GT-4, GT-5, GT-12) |
| No current CI/regression gate checks line or token count | untested belief | Read the actual gate registry and hooks | **Confirmed** | `scripts/check-body-budget.py` no longer exists on disk (GT-5); `_gate_registry.py` has no line-count gate (GT-12 context); `CLAUDE.md`'s "Key invariants" section (lines 334–341) names link resolution, skill structure, and version-stamp consistency — no line or token invariant (GT-6) |

---

## 3. Ground Truths

- **GT-1** (`?` — unverifiable from this repo) The original budget was recorded as requirement **META-Q4**: *"Agent body in `first-principles/agents/first-principles.md` stays under the ~500-line / ~5,000-token budget. New content lives in references/examples/ where appropriate."* This is quoted by the in-repo worked example at `first-principles/references/examples/self-application.md` (its own GT-7), which states the source file, `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md`, was never tracked in this repository, even at the commit it cites. I could not independently open that file — `.planning/` is gitignored and the path doesn't exist on disk. Provenance: **reported-by-delegate**, carried forward with its `?`.

- **GT-2** The numeric ceiling was raised reactively, not derived: `MAX_LINES` moved 500 → 580 (commit `65f9a4f`, "raise MAX_LINES to 580 (D-10)") → 644 (commit `981317c`, "raise MAX_LINES to 644 (D-10 redux)"), per direct `git log --oneline` read of `scripts/check-body-budget.py`'s history. Read-at-source.

- **GT-3** A blind A/B quality experiment compared a 590-line and a 612-line agent body (a 22-line contrast — the exact "buffer" the ceiling had just been raised to protect) and found: *"Arm A: 2/3 PASS, band total 35, mean 11.67. Arm B: 2/3 PASS, band total 35, mean 11.67. The arms are indistinguishable on every aggregate."* Source: `docs/v8.6-quality-ab-experiment.md`, lines 45–53, read directly. Read-at-source.

- **GT-4** On the strength of GT-2 and GT-3, the project's own governing record retired the line-count gate outright: *"The gate is retired; the figure is not... the script's own fitted-limit provenance comment... records that the number was recalibrated whenever it bound... rather than derived from any measured quality requirement."* Source: `docs/v8.7-constraint-teardown.md` §2 item 1 (lines 48–56), read directly. This record is explicitly marked a "standing rule... no expiry." Read-at-source.

- **GT-5** The reporter script itself was later fully deleted (not merely disarmed): `test ! -e scripts/check-body-budget.py` — I confirmed this directly; the file is absent from the working tree. Source: `docs/v9.4-gate-retirement.md` §2.5, corroborated by my own filesystem check. Read-at-source.

- **GT-6** The current `CLAUDE.md` "Key invariants" section (lines 334–341, read directly) names three invariants — link resolution, skill-frontmatter structure, version-stamp consistency — and contains **no** line-count or token-count invariant. The only surviving mention is a parenthetical in the hook description (line 88): "body-budget retired under TEARDOWN-01." Read-at-source.

- **GT-7** The current agent body (`first-principles/agents/first-principles.md`) measures **1,424 lines / 20,772 words** by direct `wc -l`/`wc -w`. A rough word→token estimate (×1.3) puts it near **27,000 tokens** — roughly 5.4× the original ~5,000-token figure and 2.8× the original line figure — read-at-source for the line/word counts; the token figure is an approximation, not a real tokenizer count, and is flagged as such.

## 5. Abandoned Reasoning

### Dead End: "878/1,424 lines is over budget → split the file into references/"

**What was tried:** the reflexive response the prompt names — treat the number as the signal and extract content, generically, into `references/`.

**Why abandoned:** C2 shows the overage is not where a naive split would look. The prior in-repo analysis already ran this exact play once (aggressively extracting the Phase 1-5 procedural blocks) and found it (a) saved only ~96 of the needed ~380+ lines — an arithmetic failure before any quality argument — and (b) broke the unconditional phase-ordering through-line the agent executes on every single analysis, as distinct from the conditionally-read appendix/catalog content the project's one working precedent (the assumption-taxonomy link) actually supports. Running the same play again today, against the newer 8-procedure growth, would hit the identical objection: these procedures are conditionally invoked by Step 0 routing, which is a better fit for externalization than the always-executed methodology — but that is a narrower, already-partially-applicable move, not a wholesale "split everything" response.

**What it ruled out:** generic, non-measured extraction as a response to a line-count number (GT-2, C2). Any future extraction here must be justified by which segment is duplicated, stale, or conditionally-read — not by which segment looks "proceduralist."

### Dead End: "The gates all pass today, so the size doesn't matter"

**What was tried:** treat QUAL-01 passing and the absence of any line-count failure as proof that no further attention is needed.

**Why abandoned:** this conflates "the properties we currently measure are fine" with "every property that could matter is fine." C4 names the specific gap (token/context cost) that this argument quietly waves away. The project's own history (GT-3, GT-4) shows the correct move when a concern is unmeasured is to commission a targeted measurement, not to infer safety from the passing of a differently-scoped gate.

**What it ruled out:** using "the currently-running gates pass" as a standalone argument against any further action (ruled out by C4, GT-10).

---

## 6. Conclusion

**Recommended approach:** (chains C1, C2, C3, C4) Do not split the file in response to the number. Concretely:

1. **Do not perform a generic extraction.** (chain C2) Measure which segment actually drives the overage before touching anything. In this repository, that segment was duplicated appendix content (resolved 2026-05/09) and is now newly authored feature content (two added companion techniques) — neither is a good extraction target by the "split it" reflex, and the one segment that was a good target (duplication) has already been removed.
2. **Stop trusting the line/token count as the signal of a real problem.** (chain C1) In this exact codebase it demonstrably wasn't one: the number was never tied to a stated consequence, was raised three times reactively rather than re-derived, and its only testable hypothesis (quality degradation) returned a null result. The project's own answer was to retire the gate entirely and later delete even its reporter — not to keep chasing a revised number.
3. **Replace the proxy with a direct measurement of the property that actually matters**, which this project already did: (chain C3) QUAL-01 measures analysis correctness continuously, independent of body size, rather than gating a word count that stands in for it.
4. **Commission the one measurement that remains genuinely open** (chain C4): token-cost/latency per invocation at current size vs. a de-inlined comparison. This is the one candidate property from the original five (cost, context-pressure, editability, drift-risk, review-noise) that is neither resolved nor retired — it has simply never been asked, and the project's own A/B harness could answer it cheaply.

**Key insight:** (chains C1 and C2) The reflexive "split it" response treats the budget number as self-justifying evidence of a problem. In the one case this project actually lived through, the number was over-interpreted twice: once by the team that kept raising the ceiling instead of asking what it protected, and once by whoever would now propose splitting the current 1,424-line file on the same unexamined basis. The correct move both times was the same: name the property, measure it directly, and only then decide whether extraction, retirement, or nothing is warranted — and when it is warranted, target the measured segment (duplication), not the superficially "most procedural" one.

**Trade-offs acknowledged:**

- (chain C1) The MEDIUM confidence on "the budget protects nothing real" rests on a quality A/B conducted at a narrow 22-line contrast near the old ceiling. It is strong evidence against a tight threshold effect at that scale; it is not proof that no cost exists at today's much larger scale (1,424 vs. 500 lines). Chain C4 names exactly this gap rather than hand-waving past it.
- (chain C3) Retiring the line-count gate without instituting any cost/latency measurement (only a correctness measurement) means the project traded a bad proxy for a good-but-partial direct gate — correctness is covered, cost is not.
- (chain C2) This recommendation deliberately does not re-open the already-settled appendix-duplication question; it only applies the same reasoning forward to the file's current state, where the conclusion changes because the facts have changed (duplication is gone, new inlined content is not).

**Pre-check:** head C1 (MEDIUM), C2 (HIGH), C3 (HIGH), C4 (MEDIUM) · ?-marked: none · lowest cited: MEDIUM · Inputs ceiling: MEDIUM
**Confidence:** MEDIUM overall. C2 and C3 (what's driving today's size, and that a direct-property gate replaced the proxy) are HIGH — both are plain measurements of the shipped repo state. C1 and C4 (whether the budget protected anything, and whether a different real cost still lurks at larger scale) are MEDIUM, and they are the two that should govern behavior: the recommendation is "don't reflexively split, and go measure the one thing nobody has," not "everything about file size is settled forever." The condition that would flip this recommendation: a token-cost/latency A/B at current scale showing a real, material per-invocation cost — at that point the conclusion would shift toward targeted extraction of the lowest-frequency-read segments (the companion-tool procedures, via Step 0 routing, which are already conditionally invoked) rather than a wholesale split.

20	**Section order (fixed):**
21	1. Problem Essence
22	2. Assumptions Table
23	3. Ground Truths
24	4. Derivation Chains
25	5. Abandoned Reasoning
26	6. Conclusion

28	### Document order
29	
30	The delivered file is not just these six sections — it is assembled in one absolute order: a
31	short `## Answer` block; then sections 1 through 6 above, in the fixed order and unchanged; then
32	one `## Appendix — process output` heading; then every process-output block produced during the
33	run, in the order produced, each keeping its own existing top-level heading, and the structured summary last of all.
34	
35	The `## Answer` block sits above section 1 and carries three bold lead-ins: `**Recommendation:**`
36	(1–3 sentences restating §6's `**Recommended approach:**`), `**Band (from §6):**` (§6's own
37	`**Confidence:**` band, copied verbatim), and `**Would change it:**` (the evidence or verification
38	§6 names as capable of moving the band or the recommendation). Each lead-in cites at least one
39	chain inline — `(chain Cn)` — and every chain it cites is one §6 already cites for the claim being
40	restated: the Answer states nothing §6 does not already state with the same chain. It is at most
41	120 words, is written last from the final §6 text, and is not a seventh output section. Before the
42	file is assembled, each Answer line is confirmed to restate a §6 claim and name its chain; a line
43	that does not is cut, not softened.
44	
45	**The structured summary closes the appendix.** The last process-output block in the file is
46	`## Structured summary (process output)`: that heading, then exactly one fenced `json` block,
47	and nothing after it. The block restates, in the fixed fields
48	`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/summary-schema.json` defines, decisions the six sections and
49	the process-output blocks already record — each assumption's type and verdict, each ground truth
50	and whether it was read at source, each chain's confidence and what it rests on, the dead ends,
51	the techniques applied and declined, every Self-Audit Gate scoring pass in order, whether any
52	re-entry edge fired, and the recommendation in full with its confidence and what it rests on — and it adds none:
53	every id in it is one the document uses and every value agrees with the document. A reader who
54	skips it loses nothing. It is process output, not environment state, and it is not a seventh
55	output section. The agent's final message does not carry it; the block exists only in the
56	delivered file.
57	
58	**Nothing about the environment enters the document.** The six sections above are the whole deliverable, and none of them has a slot for the state of the session that produced it. Tooling, connector, authorisation, permission, quota, configuration, model, harness and transcript state are all environment state, and none of it belongs in the analysis — not in a section, not appended after §6, not as a footnote. This exclusion is about environment-state *content*, never about physical position in the file: the trailing `## Appendix — process output` sits after §6 and carries process output — the Self-Audit Gate's verdict blocks, the closure ledger, the self-audit scan, the adversarial pass record, the structured summary — none of which is environment state, and its presence there does not reopen this rule. The class is *any* fact about the machinery rather than about the problem; it is not a list of forbidden words, and a new kind of environment fact is covered by this rule on the day it first exists. A prefix such as "Unrelated to this analysis", "Separately" or "Note:" does not make such a paragraph admissible — it marks the writer as already knowing the paragraph does not belong, which is the point at which it is dropped rather than labelled. Where environment state genuinely blocked the analysis, it is already disclosed in its proper place: a failed reference read under the template's own disclosure rule, and an unmet evidence need as a `?`-marked input carried into the Assumptions Table and named on the affected `**Confidence:**` line. Environment state that blocked nothing is reported to the user outside the deliverable, after the document ends, or not at all.

72	## 2. Assumptions Table
73	
74	List every assumption — explicit and implicit — that the analysis rests on. Classify each by type and apply the prescribed treatment. An assumption omitted from this table is an assumption that will propagate unchallenged through every later step.
75	
76	| Assumption | Type | Treatment | Verdict | Verification |
77	|------------|------|-----------|---------|--------------|
78	| [Assumption text] | [physical law / current constraint / convention / untested belief] | [prescribed action per type — see below] | [Accept / Challenge / Discard] — [justification/reason] | [source, or "unverified — flagged" if used in a chain per D-07] |
79	
80	**These five columns are the whole table — no ID column.** Assumptions are referred to by the
81	`[Assumes: A-N]` marks the chains carry and by the `A-N` labels used in the Assumption Audit
82	scan; adding a sixth ID column to this table duplicates that identity in a second place, and two
83	places that name the same thing drift. A run that adds one is deviating from this template even
84	though nothing rejects it today.
85	
86	### Type Definitions and Prescribed Treatments
87	
88	**physical law** — a constraint imposed by physics, mathematics, or formal logic that cannot change regardless of context or decisions made.
89	Prescribed treatment: accept as a ground-truth candidate and record it in the Ground Truths section.
90	
91	**current constraint** — a real limitation that applies now but could change (budget, team size, regulatory environment, technology availability).
92	Prescribed treatment: record the expiry conditions — what would have to change for this constraint to no longer hold. Do not treat it as permanent.
93	
94	**convention** — a practice or standard that exists because it has been adopted, not because it is physically or logically required.
95	Prescribed treatment: explicitly challenge the convention before accepting it. "We do it this way" is not a justification.
96	
97	**untested belief** — a claim held as true that has not been empirically verified in the context of this analysis.
98	Prescribed treatment: verify it, or flag it unverified. An untested belief used in a derivation chain must be marked with the `GT-N?` notation (see Ground Truths) and any conclusion depending on it inherits a confidence caveat.
99	
100	### Stakes-Escalation Rule
101	
102	The higher the stakes of the conclusion resting on an assumption, the more that assumption must be pushed toward physical law or verified ground truth status. Classification drives the method — it does not merely label.
103	
104	### Verdict Vocabulary
105	
106	The Verdict cell is a token prefix followed by an em-dash and the justification — the bare
107	token leads so it stays matchable, and the em-dash prose carries the reasoning. **The separator
108	is an em-dash, never a colon.** `Accept: the figure is audited` puts the token and the reasoning
109	on one side of a punctuation mark that appears throughout ordinary prose, so the cell stops being
110	matchable — which is the whole property the token-first form exists to provide. Measured: a single
111	run using the colon form scored ten non-conforming verdict cells at once. The em-dash is not a
112	stylistic preference here; it is the delimiter:
113	
114	- **Accept** — the assumption survives challenge and may be used in the analysis (e.g., "Accept — survives P2 challenge; physical-law backed by GT-1")
115	- **Challenge** — the assumption is questionable; probe further before use (e.g., "Challenge — vendor benchmark unverified, flagged GT-5?")
116	- **Discard** — the assumption is false or irrelevant; remove from the reasoning chain (e.g., "Discard — contradicted by GT-2, no longer load-bearing")
117	
118	**A current-constraint verdict records its expiry at the point of use.** An assumption classified `current constraint` is accepted only until that constraint lapses; the verdict cell says when. The expiry belongs in the em-dash justification and never in the token slot — the token slot carries one of the three tokens above and nothing else.
119	
120	**Conforming — a current constraint recording its expiry:**
121	
122	```text
123	Accept — expires at term end (1 or 3 years); until then the constraint is contractual, not physical
124	```
125	
126	**Non-conforming — the expiry hoisted into the token slot:**
127	
128	```text
129	Current constraint (expires at term end) — contractual, not physical
130	```
131	
132	The vocabulary above is unchanged because run 3 rendered four current-constraint rows conformingly on the identical prompt by putting the expiry in the justification — this is a worked example, not a schema change.

137	
138	List the irreducible, verified facts the analysis builds on. Each ground truth carries a stable identifier used by the Derivation Chains section. Once assigned, an ID does not change.
139	
140	A ground truth must pass this test: it is a fact that is true regardless of what solution is chosen, verifiable independently of the analysis, and not derived from another item on this list.
141	
142	Every ground truth carries a **provenance label** answering one question: *did this analysis read the asserted figure or wording in the cited source?* The answer decides the suffix. A citation being present is not verification — a citation can name a real document and be wrong about what is in it.
143	
144	**Verified ground truth form** (provenance `read-at-source` — no suffix):
145	
146	- **GT-1** [fact text] — source: [verification source — data, measurement, published spec, direct observation]; read-at-source: [page, table, section, or quoted passage where the figure was read]
147	- **GT-2** [fact text] — source: [verification source]; read-at-source: [where read]
148	
149	**Delegate-reported ground truth form** (provenance `reported-by-delegate` — `?` required):
150	
151	- **GT-3?** [fact text] — cited to: [source the delegate named]; reported-by-delegate: [which sub-agent, search, or summary supplied it] — cited source not opened by this analysis
152	
153	**Unverified ground truth form (D-07)** (provenance `unverified` — `?` required):
154	
155	- **GT-4?** [fact text] — unverified: [specific reason the fact could not be verified in this analysis]
156	
157	The `?` suffix signals that this ground truth has not been read at its source — whether because it is an untested belief or because a delegate reported it and nobody opened the citation. Any conclusion depending on a `GT-N?` input inherits a confidence caveat in the Derivation Chains section. The analysis may proceed with such inputs — but the uncertainty must be visible.
158	
159	**The `?` is the default.** Drop it only when the read-at-source location can be named. A delegate report counts as read-at-source only when it quotes the source's own wording and that quote was checked — not when it merely supplies a well-formed citation.

166	```

Where a count and its enumeration disagree, **the enumeration governs.** Neither an empty enumeration nor a count of zero satisfies this on its own; the named locations are the auditable part.

174	## 4. Derivation Chains
175	
176	Show how the ground truths combine into conclusions. Every conclusion offered in this analysis must have exactly one chain here — no more (no redundant restatement), no fewer (no orphaned conclusions).
177	
178	**Chain numbering convention.** Number each `### Conclusion:` block in this section `C1`,
179	`C2`, ... in document order (e.g., `### Conclusion C1: [Conclusion text]`). The §6→§4
180	closure ledger (the agent body — `SKILL.md` on the skill surface, `agents/first-principles.md` on the agent surface — "Before presenting conclusions") cites these IDs when mapping a
181	Conclusion-section (section 6) claim back to the chain in this section that established it.
182	
183	**Chain format:**
184	
185	```text
186	GT-N + GT-M → [intermediate claim] → [conclusion]
187	```
188	
189	The one-line form is the degenerate case, used only when the whole chain fits on one physical line; a chain that does not fit uses the head-plus-arrow-led form, and a hop is split rather than continued on a second line.
190	
191	Each chain must contain at least one intermediate step. A chain that goes directly from its head inputs to conclusion is incomplete — the intermediate is where the reasoning happens. The intermediate must be a new claim that could not be stated from any single head input alone. If no intermediate can be stated, the conclusion is either a restatement of a head input (trivial) or a reasoning step is missing.
192	
193	**No-wrap rule.** A hop occupies exactly one physical line. Every line after the head begins with `→` and carries exactly one complete hop; a hop is never broken across physical lines. A chain needing more hops continues on further arrow-led lines. A hop too long for comfort is SPLIT, not wrapped — the analysis renders as Markdown, so a long hop soft-wraps for the reader without breaking the form.
194	
195	```text
196	GT-1 ([brief fact label]) + GT-6 ([brief fact label])
197	→ [intermediate claim]
198	→ [further intermediate]
199	→ [conclusion]
200	```
201	
202	**Head-input rule.** The head line lists the inputs the chain consumes: each is a `GT-N` identifier (`GT-N?` when the ground truth is unverified) or a `Cn` identifier, optionally followed by a parenthesized gloss, joined to the next by `+`. The first `→` closes the head. An input carrying unparenthesized prose — `C2's threshold` — is not an identifier and does not parse; write `C2 (threshold)` in every position. The mechanical form check detects that violation only when the prose input is the last one before the first `→`; in an earlier position the check matches the well-formed remainder and scores the head conforming, so the rule binds in positions the check does not reach.
203	
204	```text
205	GT-1? ([brief fact label]) + C2 ([brief fact label])
206	→ [intermediate claim]
207	→ [conclusion]
208	```
209	
210	The head grammar governs the head line only. A hop is prose: `C2's saving` is fine after the first `→`, and is not an input reference. One exception: a hop must not begin with a `GT-N` identifier, which the form check reads as the head of a new chain and which therefore ends this one — write `→ the duty cycle stated in GT-4 is the binding term`, not `→ GT-4's stated duty cycle is the binding term`. The form check detects that violation only while fewer than two hops precede it; in a later position the check matches the preceding hops and scores the chain conforming, so the rule binds in positions the check does not reach.
211	
212	The mechanical form check additionally rejects a chain whose head or first hop closes its own sentence before the next `→`: it reads the following arrow-led line as a new statement and ends the chain there, so a chain satisfying every rule above is scored malformed for that reason alone. The check reaches only that position — a hop that closes its own sentence from the second hop onward does not change the verdict — which is why intermediate hops carry no terminal punctuation in this project's worked examples.
213	
214	**Conforming — head, then one hop per line:**
215	
216	```text
217	GT-1 (Lambda $/GB-s, AWS pricing) + GT-6 (Fargate $/vCPU-hr, AWS pricing)
218	→ Lambda costs 2.10× per unit of actual compute
219	→ sustained workloads belong on Fargate
220	```
221	
222	**Non-conforming — a hop broken across physical lines:**
223	
224	```text
225	GT-1 (Lambda $/GB-s, AWS pricing) + GT-6 (Fargate $/vCPU-hr, AWS pricing)
226	→ Lambda costs 2.10× per unit of actual compute
227	  once idle-time billing is included
228	→ sustained workloads belong on Fargate
229	```
230	
231	The continuation line does not begin with `→`, so the chain terminates at the head's first hop and what remains reads as an incomplete chain.
232	
233	**Non-conforming — the same hops rendered as a numbered list:**
234	
235	```text
236	1. GT-1 (Lambda $/GB-s, AWS pricing) + GT-6 (Fargate $/vCPU-hr, AWS pricing)
237	2. Lambda costs 2.10× per unit of actual compute
238	3. sustained workloads belong on Fargate
239	```
240	
241	A numbered list restates each hop as its own GT-headed one-hop chain, which reads as several incomplete chains rather than one complete one — the intermediate steps stop being connected to the conclusion they build toward.
242	
243	**Non-conforming — an input carrying unparenthesized prose:**
244	
245	```text
246	GT-13? (bill composition unknown) + GT-12? (duty cycle unknown) + C2's threshold
247	→ target quantity: fraction of total AWS bill removed by the migration
248	→ the bracket straddles zero, so its two ends recommend opposite actions
249	```
250	
251	`C2's threshold` is not an identifier — it is a possessive prose phrase — so the head does not parse; the third input must be written `C2 (threshold)`.
252	
253	**Conforming — the same head with the upstream chain as an input:**
254	
255	```text
256	GT-13? (bill composition unknown) + GT-12? (duty cycle unknown) + C2 (threshold)
257	→ target quantity: fraction of total AWS bill removed by the migration
258	→ the bracket straddles zero, so its two ends recommend opposite actions
259	```
260	
261	Exactly one token differs from the block above: a `Cn` identifier with a parenthesized gloss is an admissible head input, on equal footing with a `GT-N` identifier.
262	
263	**Conforming — a chain consuming only upstream conclusions:**
264	
265	```text
266	C1 (2.20× at full duty) + C2 (conditional on an unmeasured threshold) + C4 (unconditional, zero code change) + C5 (~73% ceiling, no execution-model change)

268	→ C2's saving depends entirely on a duty-cycle figure nobody has measured
269	```

271	A head may consist entirely of `Cn` inputs with no `GT-N` term. The second hop's `C2's saving` is prose, not a head input — the head-only scope note is what permits it here.

273	**Non-conforming, and undetected by the form check — the same prose input in a non-final position:**
274	
275	```text
276	GT-13? (bill composition unknown) + C2's threshold + GT-12? (duty cycle unknown)
277	→ target quantity: fraction of total AWS bill removed by the migration
278	→ the bracket straddles zero, so its two ends recommend opposite actions
279	```

Write `C2 (threshold)` wherever the input sits; the rule is the contract, and the check is a partial instrument for it.

283	**Non-conforming — a hop beginning with a GT-N identifier:**
284	
285	```text
286	C1 (2.20× at full duty) + C2 (conditional on an unmeasured threshold)

289	```
290

292	
293	**Conforming — the same hop with the identifier moved off the front:**
294	
295	```text
296	C1 (2.20× at full duty) + C2 (conditional on an unmeasured threshold)
297	→ the duty cycle stated in GT-4 is the binding term in both estimates
298	→ the bracket straddles zero, so its two ends recommend opposite actions
299	```

301	Exactly one clause is reordered and the chain is whole again; naming a ground truth inside a hop is fine, leading with its identifier is not.

303	**Non-conforming, and undetected by the form check — the GT-led hop in a later position:**
304	
305	```text

Write `→ the duty cycle stated in GT-4 is the binding term in both estimates` wherever the hop sits; the rule is the contract, and the check is a partial instrument for it.

314	**Non-conforming — the first hop closing its own sentence:**
315	
316	```text

319	→ C2's saving is real only above the duty-cycle threshold this estimate assumes

323	
324	**Conforming — the same chain with the first hop's terminal period removed:**
325	
326	```text
327	C1 (2.20× at full duty) + C2 (conditional on an unmeasured threshold)
328	→ C1's saving is unconditional and does not depend on workload shape
329	→ C2's saving is real only above the duty-cycle threshold this estimate assumes

335	
336	```text
